summary.intent: Fix Google OAuth login in the Tauri desktop app, which was failing with error 400 because the redirect URI `tauri://localhost/google-callback.html` is rejected by Google OAuth.
summary.outcome: Google OAuth login was fixed end-to-end in the dev build: a local HTTP server was introduced for the OAuth callback, Tauri event permissions were added, and a POST body parsing bug in the Rust server was resolved. Changes were committed and staged for a bugfix PR.

repo: Tauri v2 requires explicit capability grants in `apps/desktop/src-tauri/capabilities/default.json`; `@tauri-apps/api/event` listen() requires `core:event:default` which was missing.
Google OAuth client ID is `164556913424-uif44is1apnl7rqc9a2ac7vn8u9dq0ee`; authorized redirect URIs must be pre-registered in Google Cloud Console.
The desktop app is a pnpm workspace package filtered with `--filter desktop`; dev command is `pnpm --filter desktop dev` which runs `tauri dev`.
Cargo.lock can accumulate unrelated version bumps (e.g. cipherbox-fuse) during dev builds; should be excluded or selectively committed.

code.finding: `getGoogleCredential()` was using `window.location.origin` as the base for the redirect URI, which resolves to `tauri://localhost` inside a Tauri webview — a scheme Google OAuth rejects. Fixed to use a local HTTP server port instead.

Single `stream.read()` call did not reliably capture the full POST body when headers and body arrive in separate TCP segments. Fixed by reading Content-Length header first, then reading exactly that many bytes for the body.

New `start_oauth_server` command: binds to 127.0.0.1, tries preferred ports 14200/14201/14202 first (pre-registerable in Google Console), falls back to random port, serves callback HTML, auto-terminates after 120s, emits `oauth-callback` Tauri event.
`core:event:default` was missing from capabilities, blocking `listen()` calls from the webview frontend. This must be present for any `@tauri-apps/api/event` usage.
New Tauri commands must be registered in both debug and release invoke handlers.

workflow: Tauri permission errors surface at runtime in the webview with a message like `event.listen not allowed. Permissions associated with this command: core:event:allow-listen` — check capabilities JSON when this appears.
Rust TCP servers in Tauri commands must handle partial reads; a single `read()` into a fixed buffer is insufficient for HTTP POST requests where headers and body may arrive separately.
Before committing after a Tauri dev session, check `git diff Cargo.lock` — the build toolchain can silently modify it with unrelated package version bumps.

friction: `git pull` failed on first attempt due to divergent branches with no reconcile strategy configured; required manual `git fetch` + separate merge/rebase step.
App did not appear in macOS taskbar after starting dev server; required multiple retries of `pnpm --filter desktop dev` before the window appeared.

Three sequential runtime errors had to be debugged one at a time: (1) Google 400 redirect_uri error, (2) Tauri capabilities permission error, (3) `Failed to parse callback data` from incomplete TCP read.
A stale git lock file blocked the commit and had to be manually removed.
Cargo.lock accumulated an unrelated `cipherbox-fuse` version bump that had to be identified and discarded before staging.
open_items: Authorized redirect URIs `http://localhost:14200/callback`, `http://localhost:14201/callback`, `http://localhost:14202/callback` must be added to Google Cloud Console for client `164556913424-uif44is1apnl7rqc9a2ac7vn8u9dq0ee` before this works in any environment.
PR was staged and committed but the transcript ends before push and PR creation were confirmed complete.
The local OAuth HTTP server uses a fixed 120s timeout and preferred ports 14200–14202; port conflicts on developer machines or in CI could cause intermittent failures — no retry logic is in place.

The divergent branch state between local `main` and `origin/main` (1 local vs 10 remote commits) was never resolved; the feature branch was cut from the local state without reconciling upstream changes.
